To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and implemented a service-oriented scripting lan- guage for programming mobile agents, and we have encoded the lan- guage onto a process calculus to obtain a specification for the language front-end compiler and to reuse, as much as possible, the back-end compiler and the virtual machine previously developed.

we designed and developed an agent-based scripting language that integrates the service-oriented and the mobile agent paradigmas; the language was formally specified by an encoding on the process calculus, and a prototype implementation was built.

(1) a process calculus can be used to encode a service-oriented scripting programming language; (2) the process calculus encoding of the language provides a specification for its front-end compiler; (3) the process calculus virtual machine can be used for the run-time execution of the language; and (4) the encoding can be used as an implementation of the service-oriented scripting language.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) a service-oriented mobile agent language, (ii) its semantics, (iii) the specification of the front-end of its compiler, (iv) the use of a process calculus as a target language for the back-end, and (v) the development of a virtual machine for the execution of mobile agents.
the design of a language for programming mobile agent services and with the development of a compiler and a run-time system.
the development of a new scripting language for mobile agents and its compilation to a well known process calculus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mob is a service-oriented mobile agent scripting language, whose implementation is based on an existing process calculus.

the work we present here is an attempt to combine and integrate two different paradigms, the service-oriented and the mobile agents, and to provide a complete and detailed formalization of the language we propose.
Mob is a service-oriented scripting programming language for mobile agents that is based on a well studied theoretical foundation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new scripting language for mobile agents that can be compiled into an executable code that is portable across different platforms.
we have designed and developed an implementation for a service-oriented mobile agent language, which can be used in a wide range of applications.
we have developed an executable specification of a service-oriented scripting programming language for programming mobile agent systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of the mobile agent and service-oriented programming paradigms is feasible and that the encoding of a scripting language onto a process calculus provides an effective approach to develop a compiler and a run-time system.
the integration of the two paradigms, service-oriented and mobile agents, can be performed by means of a process calculus encoding.

a service-oriented mobile agent language can be encoded onto a process language, which allows us to use the existing tools and infrastructure for the process language, and thus to develop the new language in a more efficient way.
